title: einvoice conformance attestation (v1)
description: Machine-readable JSON Schema for the deterministic conformance-CLAIM attestation produced by `python3 einvoice/gen_attestation.py` / `einvoice.gen_attestation.build_attestation`. Where receipt.schema.json describes the attestation of validating ONE invoice, this describes the attestation of the TOOL's OWN published conformance claim: an envelope `{attestation: <body>, content_sha256: <hex>}` where `content_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the canonicalized body (`json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'))`, UTF-8) — byte-identical canonicalization to receipt.py. The body copies (never re-derives-approximately) numbers out of four already-drift-guarded source artifacts — export/rules.json, export/coverage.json, testsuite_conformance.json and sbom/bom.json — plus raw-bytes SHA-256 digests of the committed generated trust artifacts. There is NO wall-clock timestamp in the hashed body: identical source artifacts always yield a byte-identical attestation and content hash, which is exactly what lets a third party recompute and compare. Versioning policy mirrors the receipt/report schemas: this `$id` and the body `format` const are STABLE within v1; any BREAKING layout change bumps both ATTESTATION_FORMAT and the `$id` to `.../v2`.

attestation.description: The attested body. Its canonical serialization is what `content_sha256` hashes.

format.description: Stable attestation-format id; bound to ATTESTATION_FORMAT in einvoice/gen_attestation.py. Consumers should match on this exact string.

rules.description: Rule-set id(s) + counts, copied from export/rules.json (drift-guarded by test_export.py).

by_family.description: Deterministic tally of rule records by their `family` tag; each value is a non-negative integer count. Keys are the family ids present in export/rules.json (e.g. 'core', 'xrechnung-cius'), so the property set is open.

count.description: The artifact's own `rule_count` (the same number test_export.py pins).

rulesets.description: Sorted set of binding `source` ids the rules bind to (e.g. 'en16931-ubl', 'xrechnung-cii') — the machine ids of the rule sets under attestation.

coverage.description: Frozen coverage headline, copied verbatim from export/coverage.json (drift-guarded by test_export.py).

syntax_binding.description: Proven/total syntax-binding fractions for each syntax, copied from `syntax_binding`.

testsuite_conformance.description: In-scope UBL + CII test-suite pass rates from testsuite_conformance.json (drift-guarded by test_testsuite_conformance.py). `accepted` of `total` in-scope cases pass.

corpus.description: Pinned SHA-256 of every vendored corpus artifact, taken verbatim from sbom/bom.json (produced by gen_sbom.py's `corpus_sha256`; no second hashing path). Emitted sorted by `path`.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the vendored corpus tree, e.g. 'corpus/cen-en16931'.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 pinned for the corpus tree in sbom/bom.json.

version.description: The corpus component version string as recorded in the SBOM.

artifacts.description: Raw-bytes SHA-256 of every committed GENERATED TRUST artifact, keyed by repo-relative path (e.g. 'api_contract.json' -> hex digest). The property set is the TRUST_ARTIFACTS list in gen_attestation.py, so it is open here; each value is a lowercase hex SHA-256 string.

content_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonicalized body (json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) encoded UTF-8). Changes iff the body changes.
